newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends up but fails to close above $18 lev.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends up but fails to close above $18 lev.

text.p: IPE May Brent futures ended up just 10 cents a barrel at $17.78 on Monday after an upward correction from nine months lows hit last Friday.

Despite modest gains the contract ended well below the days highs and failed to stay above the psycologically important $18 level at the end. Some dealers expect a test soon of $17.65, the technical support level set by last Fridays low.
"We are still in a downtrend. Today doesn't change that and Brent looked weak towards the close," said a broker.
The downtrend in oil prices has wiped more than $7 a barrel off the price of Brent since January 9 this year.
"The fundamentals are still the same. There is a lot of crude, we all know that dated Brent is weak and we know there's a lot of overhang in the market" said another dealer.
The physical market for crude oil remains dogged by oversupply and a persistent lack of demand from refiners despite good margins.
Supplies of sour crude are rising and selling Brent to the U.S. remains difficult. A physical cargo of Brent crude costs about $1 a barrel below IPE May Brent.
Earlier, IPE April gas oil ended 25 cents a tonne down at $162 on Monday after slipping 50 cents near the close.
Despite modestly firmer prices, which peaked at $163 in the afternoon, gas oil remains pressured.
The low of $160.75 hit last Friday was only slightly above the $159.50 which traded about a month ago and was the lowest level since last summer.

These low levels were traded despite big demand into Asia in recent months. China saw a massive 97 percent jump in year-on-year light diesel imports to 1.27 million tonnes in January and February this year. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8145
